efficacy.magnitude_basis: ORR 46% near-loop vs 0% far-loop (p = 0.0015) against an in vitro / in silico sensitivity ranking with no predicted response rate

patient_trials.quote: The study achieved its primary endpoint, with confirmed objective response rates (ORRs) of 32% and 31% by investigator and blinded independent review, respectively, with a median progression-free survival of 5.5 months.

efficacy.quote: poziotinib sensitivity was highly dependent on the insertion location, with near-loop insertions (amino acids A767 to P772) being more sensitive than far-loop insertions, an observation confirmed clinically with ORRs of 46% and 0% observed in near versus far-loop, respectively
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Elamin 2022 (PMC9667883). NCT03066206 started 2017-03 and its 50-patient cohort had read out before the near-/far-loop split was published (Robichaux 2021, Sept 2021); the same group held both, so the clinical confirmation is a retrodiction (decision 10). Registry: no results posted (completion 2026-02-16).
efficacy.note: Near- vs far-loop split (Ba/F3 plus in silico/MD modelling) matched poziotinib ORR 46% vs 0% in NCT03066206 patients already treated; a retrodiction.
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison on a member drug at patient level: the structure-based insertion-location prediction reproduced the known poziotinib responses by subgroup of the primary ORR measure (primary endpoint itself met, 32%). Retro, never same, because the classification was built after those patients' responses were known; no prospective member-drug trial on the classification was found (the PACC trials are afatinib).
efficacy.reason: Insertion-location prediction reproduced known poziotinib responses

safety.model: EGFR L858R/T790M (H1975) and del19/T790M (HCC827) NSCLC xenografts
safety.note: Xenograft paper makes no tolerability statement; the species comparison for dacomitinib is carried by the rat/dog toxicology track.
safety.quote: The results from these studies show that PF00299804 is a potent inhibitor of EGFR-activating mutations as well as the EGFR T790M resistance mutation both in vitro and in vivo.

safety.model: EGFR del19/L858R NSCLC lines (HCC827, HCC4006) and HCC827 xenografts
safety.note: Cell lines and xenografts made no tolerability prediction; the species comparison is on the rat/dog toxicology track.
safety.quote: These preclinical evaluations support further clinical development of PF00299804 for cancers with mutations and/or amplifications of ERBB family members.

safety.confidence_note: Proxy: the GLP toxicology predates the 2005 first-in-human study (NCT00225121); the FDA review is its public record.
safety.model: Rat (6-month) and dog (9-month) repeat-dose toxicology, dacomitinib
safety.note: Rat and dog repeat-dose toxicology showed epithelial atrophy of skin, eye and gut, skin lesions and conjunctivitis before patients were dosed.
safety.short: Rat/dog tox predicted skin, gut, eye harm
safety.quote: Pfizer evaluated the toxicity of dacomitinib in GLP-compliant repeated-dose toxicity studies in rats and dogs.

safety.confidence_note: FDA multidisciplinary review read in full for sections 5.1 and 8; ILD figure from the clinical safety section.
safety.model: Rat (6-month) and dog (9-month) repeat-dose toxicology, dacomitinib
safety.note: The reviewer pairs rat/dog epithelial atrophy, skin lesions and conjunctivitis with the clinic (ARCHER 1050: grade 3-4 acneiform dermatitis 14%, diarrhoea 8%); grade 3-4 ILD in 0.5% went unpredicted.
safety.quote: Dermatologic, gastrointestinal, and ocular toxicities are also common clinical findings.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by the regulator, and the animals showed the toxicity at exposures below the clinical AUC (rat 0.5x, dog 0.14x), so the harm was predicted but the margin was not: that margin failure is recorded on the dose track (margin_stated false), the harm itself here as same. Partial because grade 3-4 ILD (0.5%) and two fatal untreated diarrhoea cases in ARCHER 1050 were not predicted; safety pharmacology found no pulmonary effect at 500 mg/kg, a silence the species could have broken, but at 0.5% I did not let it override a correct prediction of the dominant harms.

safety.model: EGFR/HER2 exon 20 insertion Ba/F3 lines, PDX and GEMM (poziotinib, in-silico pocket model)
safety.note: Mice got 5-10 mg/kg with no tolerability finding reported; the paper calls rash and diarrhoea known EGFR-TKI harms and misplaced the margin, so the harm is counted on the dose track.
safety.quote: The majority (55%) of patients received a dose reduction, with the two most common adverse events being known EGFR-inhibitor-related toxicities: skin rash and diarrhea.
safety.judgement: Decision 16: the model predicted the harm but misplaced the margin (16 mg stated tolerable), so the harm is counted once, in dose, and safety stays untested rather than contra. Grade 3+ rash 48.9% and diarrhoea 25.6% in ZENITH20-2 for the record.
safety.reason: Harm counted once, on dose track

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no tolerability finding in the abstract.
safety.model: HER2 A775_G776insYVMA patient-derived organoids and PDX (pyrotinib)
safety.note: PDX mice were dosed to regression with no body-weight, diarrhoea or other tolerability finding reported.
safety.quote: Pyrotinib showed activity against NSCLC with HER2 exon 20 mutations in both patient-derived organoids and a PDX model.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Zhou 2020; NCT02834936 has no posted results.
safety.model: HER2 A775_G776insYVMA patient-derived organoids and PDX (pyrotinib)
safety.note: Mice can show EGFR-TKI diarrhoea and the PDX paper was silent; grade 3 diarrhoea hit 20% of patients in the phase 2, the class harm that set pyrotinib's MTD in breast cancer.
safety.quote: Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or 4 occurred in 28.3% of patients, with the most common being diarrhea (20.0%; all grade 3).
safety.judgement: Same rule as the breast pan-HER tile: a mouse dosed daily to tumour regression could have shown diarrhoea or weight loss, the paper reports neither, and diarrhoea was the dominant grade 3 harm. The breast-cancer finding for pyrotinib (Ma 2017, diarrhoea DLT) would import to the same conclusion, so no imported entry is added.

safety.population: EGFR exon 20 insertion or HER2 mutation
safety.model: Hypoxia-activated prodrug in EGFR exon 20 / ERBB2-mutant patient-derived lines and xenografts (tarloxotinib)
safety.note: The model predicted less rash and diarrhoea than systemic pan-HER TKIs because the active metabolite concentrates in tumour over skin.
safety.quote: This tumor-selective delivery mechanism was designed to minimize the dose-limiting toxicities that are characteristic of systemic inhibition of wild-type EGFR.

safety.population: EGFR exon 20 insertion or HER2 mutation
safety.confidence_note: Stated comparison on one patient; registry adverse-event rows (2023) give any-grade rash in 5/11, 9/22 and 3/8 and diarrhoea in 3/11, 4/22, 5/8, all non-serious, and QT prolongation in 35 of 41 patients.
safety.model: Hypoxia-activated prodrug in EGFR exon 20 / ERBB2-mutant patient-derived lines and xenografts (tarloxotinib)
safety.note: Rash and diarrhoea stayed low-grade in RAIN-701 as the skin-sparing model predicted; QTc prolongation in 35/41 patients is a harm a mouse xenograft cannot show and was known from phase 1.
safety.short: Skin-sparing held; QTc not a mouse harm
safety.quote: This tumor response occurred with minimal on-target EGFR-related toxicity, exemplified by the absence of diarrhea and only a mild rash.
safety.judgement: The stated prediction (less wild-type EGFR toxicity) held in direction: no serious rash or diarrhoea events in the registry record versus 48.9% grade 3+ rash for poziotinib. Partial because the comparison the source states is n=1 and QT prolongation dominated the AE table; I did not score QTc against a mouse xenograft model, which cannot show it. Low confidence.

safety.model: Gefitinib-resistant ERBB2 (HER2) exon 20 insertion-mutant lung-cancer cell models (dacomitinib, Engelman 2007)
safety.quote: These preclinical evaluations support further clinical development of PF00299804 for cancers with mutations and/or amplifications of ERBB family members.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Engelman 2007 (not open access); the ERBB2-mutant work is reported as cell-based, no HER2-mutant xenograft is described in the abstract, hence model_kind ex_vivo (no cell-line enum value). Kris 2015 abstract: diarrhoea 90% (grade 3/4 20%/3%), dermatitis 73%, one death from a dacomitinib-mirtazapine interaction.
safety.note: Cell model silent on tolerability; the diarrhoea, dermatitis and one interaction death in Kris 2015 are harms a cell line cannot show.
safety.short: Cell model cannot show GI or skin toxicity
safety.judgement: A cell line cannot show diarrhoea, rash or drug interactions, so its silence is not a miss (v3 safety rule); the species comparison lives on the rat/dog toxicology track.
safety.reason: Cell line cannot show diarrhoea or rash
